title: Documenting Interfaces and Modules
story: You come back to your code after three weeks and can't remember what `Transmogrifier` does or why `validate_all` takes two parameters. Good documentation is a gift to your future self. Document your interfaces and modules clearly.
why: Clear documentation for interfaces and modules makes your code usable by others and by your future self, reducing the 'what does this do?' tax.
analogy: IKEA furniture comes with assembly instructions. Without them, you'd have a pile of screws and confusion. Interface documentation is the instruction manual: 'Here's what this does, here's how to use it, don't put the shelf on backwards.'
try_it: Take any interface you've written in previous lessons and add proper documentation comments. Include: what the interface is for, what each method does, any contracts or guarantees. Then document one of your modules with a public API summary.
tips: Document the WHAT and WHY, not the HOW — implementation can change
Include contract information in docs: what must be true before and after
A one-line summary at the top beats a novel — be concise
common_mistakes: Writing comments that describe the code (how) instead of the purpose (what/why)
Documenting obvious things while skipping the tricky parts
Letting documentation go stale — update docs when you change the code
